answer: Sybil cost scales linearly because every agent identity must bond quartz to a hardware anchor before it can transact. Two conditions hold the line: the bond is slashed when a periodic ridge challenge goes unanswered, so duplicates can't free-ride; and each proof embeds the anchor's unique quartz serial, so one cloned key can't impersonate two identities at once. Faking a thousand agents means buying a thousand anchors and stakes, not minting keys.
